precepts.text: Here's a prophecy: the Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first. So when Christ came, he wasn't going, hey, I'm just gathering all Israel. He said, no, I got to start with Judah, and then the rest of them come later on.
precepts.point: Pay attention. Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not: those Gentiles there is the northern kingdom. That's why they're in the same sentence with Samaria. Why does he stipulate the Samaritans? That was the leading tribe, Ephraim. But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel: meaning the kingdom of Judah. Start with Judah first.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Christ commanded the twelve, “Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” Those Gentiles are the northern kingdom; that's why they are in the same sentence with Samaria. He names the Samaritans because Ephraim was the leading tribe. The lost sheep there means the kingdom of Judah: start with Judah first.

Here's the prophecy of it: “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” The tents of Judah first.

So when Christ came, he wasn't going, hey, I'm just gathering all Israel at once. He said, no, I got to start with Judah, and then the rest of them come later on. That is why he held the apostles back from the Gentiles and the Samaritans in Matthew 10: the order was set by the prophet, Judah first.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

precepts.why:
Jeremiah says the Lord will gather us from all the nations whither he has driven us, and in all those nations we are hated. Christ said so himself: “And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake”. If Christ, the black Messiah himself, said I am going to be hated of all men, why am I surprised when they hate me? That shows the Christians are not reading this Bible. “but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.”

“But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.” We are not going to be able to cover the whole earth. We will not wake up every single Israelite before Christ comes back; that is what he is saying.

But the Lord will “bring you again into the place whence I caused you to be carried away captive”: Israel, Jerusalem, our land. Everything you see here is temporary. It is a movie, and you already know the end: you win. So why are you bugging out? Some of us turn to liquor and alcohol to deal with the hatred and the trauma. You have to expect the hatred. The problem is you are dying to be loved by people who are never going to love you.

precepts.point: This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, it spreads to the soldiers under him.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

precepts.why:
“And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul.” This is the level we have to get to: where we are not afraid of those brothers and sisters, and the other nations, that can kill the body and have power over us in this society.

“But rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.” That is the Lord. We need to fear the Lord, the one who can kill body and soul in hell.

Saul feared the Philistines and feared the people, and not the Lord. So, back to 1 Samuel 28:6: “when Saul enquired of the Lord, the Lord answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.” The Lord was not dealing with Saul anymore. He went to the witch at Endor, the same kind he had put out of the land, and Samuel told him, “the Lord is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy.” Because he was bashful, self-willed, easily manipulated and made excuses, he lost the kingdom. Fear the Most High, not man.

precepts.text: They which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen traveled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only: primarily dealing with Judah first.
precepts.point: Christ still went to Samaria in John 4 and taught for a few days, because he knew the time was coming to deal with them.

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

precepts.why:
“Go not into the way of the Gentiles”: in this verse that includes the other eleven tribes. “And into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not”: that is the Northern Kingdom. Why? Because it was not their time yet. The Lord said he would raise the tents of Judah first. “But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel”: that starts with Judah first.

Some are confused and think this is new. It is not; it has always been taught. Acts shows the order being followed after Christ: “Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.”

To none but the Jews only: only to Judah. They were primarily dealing with Judah first.

That does not mean the rest were never to be reached. Christ himself went to Samaria in John 4 and taught the Samaritans for a few days, because he knew the time was coming to deal with them. Judah first, and then the other tribes.

precepts.text: Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles: not of Judah only, but also the other tribes. There is no contradiction once you know the order.
precepts.point: Christ still went to Samaria in John 4 and taught for a few days, because he knew the time was coming to deal with them.

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

precepts.why:
The disciples went first to Judah, “preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.” Then watch what Paul says: “Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?”

“Even us”: the tribe of Benjamin and all the other tribes. “Whom he hath called, not of the Jews only”: not of Judah only. “But also of the Gentiles”: the other eleven tribes.

Some were perverting Zechariah 12:7, where the Lord raises the tents of Judah first, as if it meant only Judah. Judah first is the order, not the whole. So go back to Matthew 10 with a better understanding: “Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” In the beginning it was Judah first; afterward the call went to the rest of the tribes. There is no contradiction once you know the order.

precepts.text: They have taken crafty counsel against thy people: slavery, miseducation and a religion that teaches death is the end and hell waits, so everybody is afraid to die.
precepts.point: The hairs of your head are numbered and you are of more value than sparrows. Whosoever confesses me before men under tribulation I will confess, and whosoever denies me under torture, my husband forced me, I never believed it, I will deny.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Christ says, “And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul”. They can't kill the real you, brothers and sisters. You think that body is the real you, but it is just a shell that corrodes in time. So why is our people so afraid to die? David shows it: “They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones.”

Slavery, miseducation and religion are all part of that crafty counsel. Their religions make you think this is all there is, like the Sam Cooke song: I don't know what's up there beyond the sky. It puts a spirit of fear on you: if you die, you're going to hell and you're going to burn down there. So everybody is afraid to die.

But when you read the Bible, how come our foremothers and forefathers did not have the spirit we have today? They knew something we don't. The woman with the seven sons said, kill me now, cut my arms off, cut my tongue. We say, what the hell is this? Because the crafty counsel taught us lie after lie about reality: that after this you're done.

The Bible calls death sleep, many times. That's all it is, and you wake up before the Lord. Paul said to be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord. But do we believe that, or what the white man says on his television screens?

Christ goes on, “but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell”: that is the lake of fire, which is not now. When you die now, everybody is at rest, even the wicked. When the Lord returns he takes the keys of hell and death and opens it all up, and that is when the lake of fire comes. So don't fear them that kill the body, because the things we teach will get us killed, and you will not deny Christ if you have not swallowed their crafty counsel.

precepts.text: Paul shut up the saints in prison, gave his voice against them when they were put to death, punished them in every synagogue and compelled them to blaspheme, exceedingly mad against them even unto strange cities: what he did the Pharisees and later the inquisitors under Ferdinand and Isabella all did, and it is what Christ said denying him under persecution looks like. Some here are hirelings who will fold.
precepts.point: The hairs of your head are numbered and you are of more value than sparrows. Whosoever confesses me before men under tribulation I will confess, and whosoever denies me under torture, my husband forced me, I never believed it, I will deny.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Christ says, “But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.” Under what conditions? Not at work saying, yeah, I believe in God. Read in context, it is tribulation, persecution, Jacob's trouble: I never believed that Israelite stuff, I don't believe in those commandments, my husband forced me, my wife forced me.

Paul testified what denying looks like from the persecutor's side: “Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.”

“And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme”. Compel means he forced them to blaspheme. That is what Christ was talking about: deny me under torture, persecution, tribulation, hard times. That is the trial all of us alive at this time must go through.

Paul was not the only persecutor. What Paul did, they were all doing: the Pharisees, and later the inquisitors under Queen Isabella and King Ferdinand in the time of Spain and Portugal, whose job was to hunt down Israelites keeping the commandments, to Africa, to Mexico, to South and North America.

And “being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.” That is why Christ said, when they persecute you in this city, flee into another.

Everybody in here says they love God, but some of us are liars. Some are not valiant for the truth; you are a professional student, a hireling. The hireling sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep. Think about being compelled to blaspheme, as in the film Unthinkable, where they brought in a man's wife and kids to make him confess. You think that could never happen to you; the devil is a liar. What Paul was doing is what Christ said is going to happen.

precepts.text: Whosoever confesses me before men I will confess before my Father, and whosoever denies me I will deny: under tribulation and Jacob's trouble.
precepts.point: For God is your guide, and the guide of them that keep my commandments; let not your sins weigh you down. We do sin, and if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves, but if we confess he is faithful to forgive; that is the difference between us and the Christian who teaches sin has no consequences. Let not your iniquities lift up themselves, for woe to them that are bound with their sins, covered as a field with thorns that no man can travel through, left undressed and cast into the fire. When you are bound, there is no magic scripture; you have to want to be released.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
“Then shall they be known, who are my chosen; and they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.” That verse is very important, because it goes back to what Christ said: “Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven. But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.”

Christ is talking about tribulation, persecution, Jacob's trouble. So what will the chosen be saying about Christ in that day, will they deny him or confess him? They are going to confess him.

Why does it say “Then shall they be known”? Because right now everybody says they believe in the Lord. Women say it; men say it. But when this starts to happen, you are going to see who is real and who is fake. On that day the ones who confess Christ before their tormentors are the ones known to be his chosen, tried as gold in the fire, and he will confess them before his Father.

Christians say that means you cannot pay your bills and you have to carry all your problems on your back. No, that is not what it is talking about. When Christ was carrying the cross, where did it lead him? To death. He is saying the same thing for us.

We have to be willing to sacrifice ourselves. That is what Wisdom of Solomon was just saying: the souls of the righteous who die for the truth are in the hand of God. If you cannot confess the Lord, even unto death, you are not worthy to be his disciple. That is the cross, and that is how the chosen will be known.

When they persecute you in this city, flee into another: check the real estate, citizenship, and residency when you travel, because one city may pop off and the next may not. precepts.point: Alas, for that day is great, so that none is like it; it is even the time of Jacob's trouble, but he shall be saved out of it. That is the great tribulation.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
“Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he shall be saved out of it.” That is the great tribulation. Jeremiah does not go into much detail on how he is saved out of it, so Christ fills it in.

“And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.” Christ prophesied we would be hated of all men for his sake, so we have to endure the hatred. Brothers and sisters on TikTok, YouTube and Instagram ask why the white man hates us so much. Because we are the sons and daughters of God, the people of Christ.

“But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another”. So when you brothers go to these other countries, check out the real estate, find out whether you can get citizenship or residency, question and research, because if something pops off here we have to be able to move. One city may pop off and the next city may not have the same persecution.

“for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.” We will not have reached all the twelve tribes before Christ comes; we are not going to reach every Israelite. Christ says the same in Matthew 24: they shall deliver you up to be afflicted and kill you, many shall be offended and betray one another, but he that endures unto the end, either your death or Christ's return, shall be saved.

precepts.text: Ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles.
precepts.point: The Lord consumes him with the spirit of his mouth, speaking through his witnesses, and destroys him with the brightness of his coming.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
“And ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles.” We are going to be brought before governors and kings as a testimony against them. The testimony is us teaching the Bible, the laws and the testimonies, letting them know: God is coming back to destroy you. You are wicked. You have been stealing land, you have been murdering, you are the wicked of the earth.

When you testify on this earth, you are condemning people. Everybody who hears the word of God and turns their back on it is condemned. Every white person hearing about the Israelites and hearing these teachings, many of them online, is hearing that the Lord is going to judge Edom and judge Amalek, and those who call themselves Jews and are not. We are bringing forth judgment on the earth.

“But when they deliver you up, take no thought how or what ye shall speak: for it shall be given you in that same hour what ye shall speak. For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.” Do not worry what to say before kings. It will not be you speaking; the spirit that dwells in us takes over, and it is the Lord judging them with your voice.

That is how the Lord consumes the wicked “with the spirit of his mouth.” 2 Esdras 11 shows it too: the roaring lion that sends out a man’s voice unto the eagle, which is Rome, with Europe and America as its extension. That voice is the prophets, the witnesses on the earth today, condemning Edom for all the evil he has done through the centuries.

precepts.text: Confess Christ before men though it set you at variance with your own household; he that loveth father or mother more than Him is not worthy of Him.
precepts.point: Confessing Christ before men means something. When Christ asked, Whom say ye that I am, Peter confessed, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God; whoever confesses Him before men, He confesses before His Father, and He came to set a man at variance against his own household for the truth's sake.

note.label: Genesis 12: The Calling of Abram

precepts.why:
Getting out from your kindred and your father's house is what Christ asks too. “Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven. But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.” Confessing Christ before men means something.

“Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.” He came to set a man at variance against his own household for the truth's sake.

“He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.” As Abram left his kindred when he was called, do not let family or friends hold you back from the call.

precepts.point: Christ came not to send peace on earth but a sword, setting a man at variance against his own household; he that loveth father or mother more than him is not worthy of him. note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

precepts.why:
Phinehas was zealous for his God among the people, and the Lord gave him His covenant of peace. Being zealous today is confessing Christ before men.

“Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven. But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.” You confess him mainly through your actions, and his steps were keeping the commandments of God; the first way you deny Christ is by rejecting the commandments.

For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.”

We stay zealous by letting nothing separate us from following Christ in his steps: keeping the laws of God, teaching the gospel, and spreading the word with wisdom.

If the Lord finds you lukewarm, choosing your kids, your parents, or your spouse over following God and Christ and keeping the commandments wholly, you will not enter into the land, as that whole generation did not. You must follow fully like Caleb and zealously like Phinehas; nothing may keep you from following fully.

note.label: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People

Christ laid it out: “Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.”
